summary: Settings-file existence check and cleanup. Resolves the target file path into lpFileName via sub_4B9830, falling back to the default path byte_5EA438 when the resolver returns null. Opens the path with the read-mode string aRb through sub_587DB0; only when the open succeeds does it close the handle (FileCloseWithLock), clear the read-only attribute (ToggleFileReadOnlyAttributeViaWin32API with attribute constant 128), and delete the file (FileDeleteWithErrorHandling), recording success in v0. The returned bool is !v0, so the function reports true when no file existed (or deletion failed) and false when a file existed and was deleted. The heap-allocated path buffer lpFileName[0] is released via FreeWrapper_7bcf when non-null.

local_names.v0: records that an existing file was found and deleted successfully
local_names.v1: resolved file path (lpFileName[0] or default byte_5EA438)
local_names.v2: open handle / success indicator returned by sub_587DB0
local_names.v3: inverted result returned to the caller
local_names.lpFileName: two-slot buffer; slot 0 holds the resolved heap-allocated path, slot 1 is initialized to -1

operations.description: Initialize local state: v0 = false, lpFileName[0] = null, lpFileName[1] = -1 before the path is resolved.
sub_4B9830(lpFileName) resolves the settings-file path into the buffer; on success slot 0 receives the heap-allocated path string.
v1 = lpFileName[0]; when the resolved path is null, v1 falls back to the default path string byte_5EA438.
v2 = sub_587DB0(v1, aRb) attempts to open the path using the read-mode string aRb; a non-zero v2 indicates the file exists and was opened.
Deletion path runs only when v2 is non-zero (open succeeded); otherwise the function skips cleanup and reports that no file existed.
FileCloseWithLock(v2) closes the opened file handle.
ToggleFileReadOnlyAttributeViaWin32API(v1, 128) clears the read-only attribute (constant 128) on the path so deletion can succeed.
v0 = (FileDeleteWithErrorHandling(v1) == 0); a zero return from the delete wrapper sets v0 to true, marking a successful delete.
v3 = !v0 inverts the delete result: the function returns true when no file existed or deletion failed, false when a file existed and was deleted.
When lpFileName[0] is non-null, the resolver allocated a path buffer that must be released.
FreeWrapper_7bcf(lpFileName[0]) frees the heap-allocated resolved path buffer.
return v3 (true = no existing file or deletion failed; false = file existed and was deleted).
Invoked by GameDataFileIO (004b7300) and sub_4B7500 (004b7500) as part of the file/settings cleanup flow.
